messages:
jessica (Platform): FYI starting a short design thread for the on-prem metrics forwarder we need for Private customers. Goal: single lightweight agent that ships runtime+infra metrics out over TLS to customer endpoints (S3/syslog/HTTPS) with KMS-wrapped creds and audit hooks. Want input on firewall/egress, KMS patterns, and console dashboard mapping.

mike (Infra): +1. do we expect customers to open egress to our hosted collector or will agent push directly to customer destinations? big difference for firewall rules.

jessica (Platform): Primary pattern: agent -> customer-managed collector (preferred for compliance). We also need an opt-in 'relay' mode for cases where customers can't run a collector. Relay would be deployed into their VPC with strict routing.

tanvi (Security): For customer-managed collector pattern, we need to avoid storing long-lived secrets on the agent. Outline: agent uses ephemeral credentials fetched from control plane, wrapped by customer's KMS (if they request). Audit hooks must emit an audit event on key unwrap. Thoughts? :lock: 

samir (Runtime): Can the agent read runtime labels (model id, node id, instance type) from the serving runtime without adding heavy dependencies? We prefer a simple file/socket API. Also need to preserve sampling/rollout tags so dashboards can filter by rollout_id.

mike (Infra): Firewall rules: customers typically only allow outbound 443 to a few IPs. Recommend documenting both DNS and IPs and providing an option to send to an IP:443 or host header for collector. Example rule we tested:

```
# allow agent outbound to collector IP
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 10.2.3.45 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
```

We should also support proxy env vars for corp proxies.

tanvi (Security): KMS: customers may want to use their own KMS or our hosted KMS. For BYOK we need a flow like: agent requests a one-time bearer nonce from control plane, CP returns a data key encrypted with customer KMS, agent unwraps locally. CP emits audit log: `kms:EncryptDataKey` and `kms:DecryptRequest`. We'll need a hook so customers can pipe those audit events into their SIEM.

jessica (Platform): Good. For audit hooks we can either POST to an audit webhook or stream via syslog. Which do people prefer?

eva (DevEx): Webhook is easier to integrate into our console for showing recent key unwraps per customer; syslog option is fine for heavy-security customers. We should keep both. UI needs a per-customer audit timeline in Console > Private > Exports.

samir (Runtime): On tags/labels — runtime can expose a small metadata socket `/var/run/rw-metadata.sock` with newline-delimited `key=value` pairs. Agent can read and attach these as metrics dimensions. Works for mutltiple runtimes.

mike (Infra): Relay mode: if we run a relay in customer VPC, that relay needs IAM role to push to our hosted collector. Firewall-wise, we'd only require inbound from agent on a private port and outbound 443 to our hosted endpoints. Need clear docs for security groups and NACLs.

tanvi (Security): Also need a clear threat model doc: what happens if relay/agent is compromised? Limit the scope: agent can only read metrics + metadata socket. No access to model weights or arbitrary files. KMS unwrap should be rate-limited and logged.

jessica (Platform): Dashboard mapping: propose these metric namespaces be present in Console: `redwood.runtime.tokens`, `redwood.runtime.latency.p50/90/99`, `redwood.infra.gpu.util`, plus dimensions `deployment_id, rollout_id, model_family, region`. Any other must-haves?

eva (DevEx): Add `exporter.mode` dimension (`direct` vs `relay`) so tenants can see which path produced metrics. Also we should expose agent version for debugging.

mike (Infra): Implementation checklist from infra side: 1) agent egress modes + proxy support, 2) relay helm chart + IAM role docs, 3) CI test harness for firewall scenarios.

tanvi (Security): Security checklist: 1) BYOK KMS flow doc + audit webhook, 2) default deny for any file access from agent, 3) incident playbook for compromised agent.

samir (Runtime): Runtime items: 1) metadata socket spec, 2) metric naming convention doc, 3) lightweight auth header (`X-RW-Agent:` with transient token).

jessica (Platform): Owners: Mike -> infra checklist, Tanvi -> security checklist, Samir -> runtime spec, Eva -> console mapping and audit UI. I'll draft a short RFC with these checklists and a proposed timeline (2 weeks design, 3 weeks implementation).

ops-bot: Deployment job `agent-sanity-check` finished: 3 tests passed, 1 flaky egress test (timeout). See CI: https://ci.internal/runs/4823

mike (Infra): noted the flaky egress test, I'll look at it tomorrow. Can we add a simple connectivity tester to the agent that logs a short traceroute to audit events when connectivity fails?

tanvi (Security): +1 on traceroute logs but redact any internal IPs before sending to hosted systems. For customer-managed collector path keep raw logs local and only emit redacted indicators to our control plane.

jessica (Platform): Action items: Mike/Tanvi/Samir/Eva owners as above. I'll create RFC and a hackpad with the firewall snippets, KMS sequences, and sample syslog/webhook payloads. Meeting in 48h to review RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike (Infra): thanks, will start the relay chart skeleton tonight.

samir (Runtime): I'll push the metadata socket spec and a small reference lib for the agent to read tags.

eva (DevEx): I'll draft the Console wireframes and how audit events surface.

jessica (Platform): Great, closing the loop here. If anyone hits compliance edge-cases ping me directly.
